title: Variables & Data Types
description: Master Robot Framework's variable system, including scalar, list, and dictionary variables, along with data type handling, variable scopes, and built-in variables for cross-platform test development.
learningObjectives: Create and use scalar variables with the Set Variable keyword
Manipulate strings through concatenation and composition
Work with list variables using indexing and Collections library keywords
Create and access dictionary variables for structured data
Capture keyword return values and use the Evaluate keyword for calculations
Leverage built-in variables (${CURDIR}, ${OUTPUT_DIR}, ${/}) for portable tests
Understand variable scopes: test, suite, and global
Handle different data types and perform type conversions
Build cross-platform tests using path-related built-in variables

keyTakeaways: Scalar variables use ${name} syntax and store single values
List variables use @{name} syntax and support zero-based indexing: ${list}[0]
Dictionary variables use &{name} syntax for key-value pairs
Access dictionary values with dot notation (${dict.key}) or brackets (${dict}[key])
Variables created in test cases are test-scoped (don't carry over to next test)
Suite variables (*** Variables *** section) are available to all tests in the file
The Set Variable keyword assigns values; most keywords return values
Evaluate executes Python expressions for calculations and transformations
Built-in variables (${CURDIR}, ${/}, etc.) enable cross-platform tests
Collections library provides powerful operations for lists and dictionaries
Use ${/} for path separators to ensure Windows/Linux/Mac compatibility
String concatenation uses Set Variable with variable substitution
commonPitfalls: Forgetting the $ prefix in variable syntax (writing 'name' instead of '${name}')
Confusing variable scopes (expecting test variables to persist across tests)
Using wrong prefix: ${list} vs @{list} or ${dict} vs &{dict}
Index out of range errors when accessing list items
Accessing dictionary keys with special characters using dot notation
Comparing numbers as strings instead of using Should Be Equal As Numbers
Hard-coding paths instead of using ${CURDIR} and ${/}
Forgetting that Evaluate executes arbitrary Python code (security risk)
Missing ${/} when building file paths (concatenating paths without separator)
Type mismatches when using Evaluate (string '10' vs integer 10)

realWorldApplications.description: Use dictionaries for request payloads, capture response objects, extract data with list indexing, and validate status codes
Store test users in lists, iterate with FOR loops, manage user profiles with dictionaries
Build portable file paths using ${CURDIR} and ${/} that work on Windows, Linux, and Mac
Load environment-specific settings from dictionaries, use Evaluate for conditional logic
Use Evaluate with timestamps to create unique usernames, emails, and test artifacts
Store query results in lists, validate row counts with Get Length, check data integrity with assertions
Build locator paths using string concatenation, validate multiple elements with list iteration
Use ${OUTPUT_DIR}, ${TEST_NAME}, and ${SUITE_NAME} to organize screenshots in logical directory structures
